solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Pretty person in water ignoring bachelor by river

indicators.note: by means next to, so the river abbreviation sits beside the rest
ignoring means the bachelor letter is left out of the swimmer word

parts.note: a bather is someone in the water
B is the abbreviation for bachelor, as in a BA degree

explanation.surface: Someone admires a good-looking swimmer, unattached, lounging by the river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pretty' looks like an adjective describing the person, but it is the adverb, as in 'pretty good'.
explanation.definitionFit: As adverbs of degree the two are synonyms: 'pretty tired' and 'fairly tired' mean the same.

clue.text: Criticism for interrupting retired tennis player mounting

indicators.note: interrupting means the word for 'for' breaks into the player's name
in a down clue, mounting means the name is read upwards, i.e. backwards

parts.note: Rod Laver, the retired Australian tennis champion
pro means for, in favour of

explanation.surface: A retired tennis star climbs into the stand and gets criticised for interrupting play.
explanation.walkthrough: Rod Laver is the Australian who won the Grand Slam twice in the 1960s.
explanation.definitionFit: A reproval is a rebuke or scolding, a synonym of criticism.

clue.text: American eyed nasty game

definitions.meaning: in US informal speech a tornado, a destructive storm with an eye
the party game played on a spotty mat where players contort their limbs

explanation.surface: An American glares at someone in a nasty game.
explanation.walkthrough: 'eyed' is not a verb here: the first definition describes a violent storm that has an eye at its centre.
explanation.definitionFit: The US slang for a tornado and the Hasbro party game share one name.

clue.text: Fussy Greek character with appropriate drink served up

indicators.note: in a down clue, served up means the assembled pieces are read upwards, i.e. backwards

parts.note: eta is a letter of the Greek alphabet
to appropriate is to take, i.e. rob
ale is a drink

explanation.surface: A fussy Greek takes his own drink and it is served to him.
explanation.definitionFit: Elaborate means highly detailed and ornate, close to fussy in design.

clue.text: With roughly tenth disappearing, street urchins cooked beetles

indicators.note: roughly says the letters of tenth are taken out in any order, not as a run
disappearing means those letters vanish from the larger pool
cooked means the remaining letters of street urchins are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written as the letter pool
taken as written; its letters are removed

explanation.surface: Street children cook up a meal of beetles while a tenth go missing.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove T, E, N, T, H from STREET URCHINS ('roughly' ... 'disappearing'), leaving SRUERCIS, which 'cooked' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: To beetle along is to scurry, a verb sense of the insect's name.

clue.text: Caught three times, your turmoil is shown in diversion for roundabout

indicators.note: diversion suggests things sent off their course, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: C is the cricket abbreviation for caught, taken three times
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A cricketer caught out three times in the turmoil looks for a roundabout diversion.
explanation.definitionFit: Circumlocutory speech goes round the houses, being indirect or roundabout.

clue.text: Traditional meal from pasta — no tips required

indicators.note: no tips means each word loses its first and last letters

explanation.surface: A diner wants a traditional meal made from pasta, without tipping.
explanation.walkthrough: fRoM and pAsTa lose their ends, giving RO and AST.
explanation.definitionFit: A Sunday joint of roasted meat is the classic traditional British meal.

clue.text: Write misentries penning record

indicators.note: penning means enclosing, so the letters sit inside the words written out

explanation.surface: A clerk keeps writing wrong entries while penning the record.
explanation.definitionFit: To record each point separately on a list is to list them one by one.

clue.text: Mangy bears start to perish fast

indicators.note: bears means carries, so the shabby word holds the extra letter

parts.note: mangy means shabby, i.e. seedy

indicators.note: start to means the first letter of the next word

explanation.surface: Mangy bears are starting to die off fast.
explanation.definitionFit: Speedy and fast are synonyms for quick.

clue.text: Don, a shade upset, considered royal rebuke

parts.note: to don clothes is to wear them

indicators.note: in a down clue, upset means turned upside down, i.e. reversed

parts.note: a tone is a shade of colour
mused means considered, pondered

explanation.surface: Someone puts on a slightly upsetting colour and earns a royal rebuke.
explanation.walkthrough: The famous line is attributed to Queen Victoria.
explanation.definitionFit: Queen Victoria's legendary put-down is the archetypal regal reprimand.

clue.text: Vessel's solitary lug pronounced

indicators.note: pronounced means spoken, so the phrase is heard rather than read

parts.note: solitary means private and lug is British slang for ear: private ear

explanation.surface: A lonely sailor's ear is described as prominent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lug' is British slang for an ear.
explanation.definitionFit: A privateer was a privately owned armed ship licensed to attack enemy shipping.

clue.text: Singer from Aussie city needing no help

indicators.note: needing no means the word for help is dropped from the city

parts.note: Adelaide is the capital of South Australia
aid means help

explanation.surface: A singer from an Australian city performs without support.
explanation.definitionFit: The British singer-songwriter famous for 'Someone Like You' is an example of a singer.

clue.text: Best soldiers in open air

parts.note: to best someone is to beat or outdo them
OR stands for other ranks, i.e. ordinary soldiers

explanation.surface: The finest troops are deployed in the open.
explanation.definitionFit: Something happening outside in the fresh air rather than indoors is described this way.

clue.text: New free bags are unlimited

indicators.note: bags means holds inside, so the freed word contains the extra letter

parts.note: untied means free, loosed

indicators.note: unlimited means the word loses its outer letters

explanation.surface: New free carrier bags are available without limit.
explanation.definitionFit: Untested and new both describe something not yet tried out.

clue.text: A hassle dispatching large containers of claret

indicators.note: dispatching means sending away, so the large abbreviation is removed

parts.note: a trial is a hassle, a nuisance
L is the clothing-size abbreviation for large

explanation.surface: Getting rid of big wine containers is a hassle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Claret' is slang for blood, not wine here.
explanation.definitionFit: The upper chambers of the heart hold blood, which old boxing slang calls claret.

clue.text: Not any more openings in Nevada, Louisiana and Oregon for relocation

indicators.note: relocation means moving letters to new places, so they are rearranged
openings means the first letters of the state names

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone no longer relocating to three American states.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means formerly but not now, the same as 'not any more'.

clue.text: Fire on a makeshift American base

indicators.note: makeshift means improvised, so the letters are put together anew

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone opens fire on a temporary US military base.
explanation.walkthrough: 'base' looks like a military camp but is the adjective meaning low or wicked.
explanation.definitionFit: Base in the sense of morally low is a synonym of wicked or villainous.

clue.text: Humble before Newton, having expert around

indicators.note: around means the expert word surrounds the others

parts.note: deft means skilful, expert
ere is a poetic word for before
N is the symbol for the newton, the unit of force

explanation.surface: A humble student bows before Newton with an expert nearby.
explanation.definitionFit: Deferent is an uncommon variant of deferential, meaning respectful and submissive.

clue.text: Choose about one hundred mice, endlessly diverse

indicators.note: about means the choosing word goes round the numeral

parts.note: to elect is to choose
C is the Roman numeral for one hundred

indicators.note: endlessly means the word loses its first and last letters

explanation.surface: Someone picks out about a hundred mice of varied kinds.
explanation.definitionFit: An eclectic collection draws from many different sources, so it is varied.

clue.text: Jockey is on this horse for horse-racing, perhaps

indicators.note: to jockey is to manoeuvre, so the letters are moved about

parts.note: the letter pool, taken as written
taken as written, the letters that join the answer

explanation.surface: A jockey rides a horse in a race.
explanation.walkthrough: A composite anagram: 'Jockey' rearranges the answer plus IS ON into HORSE-RACING, so remove I, S, O, N from HORSE-RACING and rearrange the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: A charger is a cavalry or war horse, so it is a kind of horse.

clue.text: Bishop wears light make-up

indicators.note: wears means has on, so the light word holds the bishop letter

parts.note: to light is to fire, set alight
B is the chess abbreviation for bishop

explanation.surface: A bishop puts on light cosmetics.
explanation.walkthrough: 'make-up' is not cosmetics but character, as in moral fibre.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone's moral fibre is their essential character or constitution.

clue.text: Poet's ordered hugging outfit for party

indicators.note: hugging means holding close, so the outfit word sits inside

parts.note: bade, past of bid, is the literary word for ordered
a rig is an outfit of clothes

explanation.surface: A poet requested a clingy outfit for a party.
explanation.definitionFit: A brigade is a group organised for a task, as in fire brigade, i.e. a party.

clue.text: Like to eat grain and fruit

indicators.note: to eat means to take in, so the comparison word holds the grain

parts.note: as means like
corn is grain

explanation.surface: Someone likes to eat grain and fruit.
explanation.definitionFit: The oak's nut is botanically its fruit.

clue.text: Maritime town's gossip — boat-builder's son

parts.note: to chat is to gossip
Ham was a son of Noah, who built the ark

explanation.surface: The talk of a port town concerns a shipwright's son.
explanation.walkthrough: Chatham, in Kent, is famous for its historic naval dockyard.
explanation.definitionFit: This Kentish town on the Medway was long home to a Royal Navy dockyard.

clue.text: Is planning to do pranks

definitions.meaning: has something scheduled, as in 'she has a meeting on'
plays tricks on, as in 'he is having you on'

explanation.surface: Someone is planning to play practical jokes.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrasal verb means both having something arranged and teasing someone.

clue.text: Make mistake piercing metal finish of the dish

indicators.note: piercing means going into, so the mistake word goes inside the metal

parts.note: tin is a metal
to err is to make a mistake

indicators.note: finish of means the last letter of the word that follows

explanation.surface: A cook errs by putting a hole in the metal finish of the dish.
explanation.definitionFit: A terrine is both the earthenware dish and the pâté cooked in it.

clue.text: Tears from opponents after scrap

indicators.note: after means the opponents follow the scrap

parts.note: a rag is a scrap of cloth
East and South are opposing partnerships at bridge

explanation.surface: Tears are shed by opponents after a fight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tears' is the verb as in tearing about, not weeping; 'scrap' is a scrap of cloth, not a fight.
explanation.definitionFit: To rage and to tear are both to rush about wildly.

clue.text: Replacement rug a store ordered

indicators.note: ordered means put in a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A shop orders a replacement rug.
explanation.definitionFit: A surrogate is a substitute standing in for someone or something.

clue.text: Sing to a daughter in calm surrounding

indicators.note: surrounding means the calm word goes round the rest

parts.note: serene means calm

explanation.surface: A parent sings to a daughter in calm surroundings.
explanation.definitionFit: To serenade someone is to perform music for them, typically under their window.

clue.text: Way up a nose

parts.note: nose means scent, as in a wine's bouquet

explanation.surface: A nose is the way to go up.
explanation.definitionFit: An ascent is a climb or upward path.
